text:
The purity of form
and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are not two, are not divided, and are not distinct.
The noble truths
and the concentrations
and the immeasurables
and the formless absorptions
and the liberations
and the serial absorptions
and emptiness
and signlessness
and wishlessness
and the higher knowledges
and the meditative stabilities
and the dhāraṇī gateways
and the powers of the tathāgatas
and the fearlessnesses
and the detailed and thorough knowledges
and great love
and great compassion
and the distinct attributes of a buddha are pure.
The purity of the sensory element of the mental faculty, the sensory element of mental phenomena, and the sensory element of mental consciousness is the purity of the sensory element of mental contact that arises from the condition of the coming together of the three.
The purity of the sensory element of mental contact that arises from the condition of the coming together of the three is the purity of the sensory element of the feeling that arises from the condition of the coming together of the three.
The purity of the sensory element of the feeling that arises from the condition of the coming together of the three is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects.
Thus, the purity of the distinct attributes of a buddha,
the purity of the sensory element of mental contact that arises from the condition of the coming together of the three,
and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects are indivisible, not two, and cannot be divided into two, and they are not distinct.
This virtue is the killing of the step.
